title: PROFINET: Update SXP dissectors
description:
The PROFINET specification received an update which makes it necessary to adjust some PDUs and the FrameID for SXP.

Include more detailed dissection of service data and SXP-relevant blocks. Also dissect the RTA header properly for SXP via RTAv3.

AI-Assisted: yes \[GH Copilot for repetitive tasks\]

notes.body:
added 2 commits
  • d55cdba6 - 1 commit from branch wireshark:master
  • 31618696 - PROFINET: Update SXP dissectors
[Compare with previous version](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/23905/diffs?diff_id=1704783727&start_sha=a6b7b11002c2763da18f5db9eabfc2dbc2cb40f9)
Wouldn't it be better to use one of the proto_tree_add_bitmask_list() functions for these constructs trougout?

Thank you for this. Not only does it make the code way cleaner, it also looks way better in the application. Got caught up with manual dissection... Implemented where applicable, also added bitmasks to the corresponding fields. Feel free to reopen if it doesn't look right to you.

changed this line in [version 4 of the diff](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/23905/diffs?diff_id=1706927000&start_sha=a43481a3915f7fd5901f8510a5aeb8df72fbe3fe#3b74a37c6d053096b92c4a2a8b69084a0d275a94_1016_1053)
As mentioned in the PR description, it's been removed from the specification and the index 0x0E is now part of a "reserved" field. Can re-introduce it to be able to dissect it for older standards.
it will broke some old pcap dissection ? you can add Reserved (Connect:...)

You are right. It will not find a corresponding PNIO status for the affected code1 values then and the reserved values have never been part of the `pn_io_error_code1_pnio`, which I thought is ok behavior for an error code not relevant anymore.

Thinking about it again I come to the conclusion that it would be good to keep the old error code to be able to dissect it in older PROFINET versions as long as it's not being reused. Thanks for your feedback!
I will close this for now, please reopen if you want another solution for this.
